name: Wang Yiping
current_role: Chairman and co-controlling shareholder, Ningbo Jifeng Auto Parts Co. (SSE: 603997)
profile: Wang Yiping is chairman and, with Wu Bifeng and Wang Jimin, the actual controller of Ningbo Jifeng Auto Parts, a headrest and seating-component maker founded in Ningbo's Beilun district. Jifeng bought control of German seating supplier Grammer AG in 2019, turning it into a global auto-interior group now pushing into complete passenger-car seats.
interesting_fact: Jifeng completed its takeover of Germany's Grammer AG (an 84% stake) in 2019, buying a much larger European commercial-vehicle seat and headrest leader and becoming one of the world's top headrest suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Jifeng, Wang worked at the Daishan cement plant and the enterprise office of Nizhi town in Daishan county (an island county in Zhoushan), per the company's 2025 annual report.
notes: Low public profile; no personal media presence found. Best route is via Jifeng board office (IR email). Not to be confused with Joyson's Wang Jianfeng (also Ningbo).

name: Deng Longjiang
current_role: Professor, UESTC School of Electronic Science and Engineering; CAE academician; actual controller of Chengdu Jiachi Electronic Technology (JC Technology, SSE STAR: 688708)
profile: Deng Longjiang (b. 1966, Anyue, Sichuan) is a UESTC materials scientist specialising in electromagnetic radiation-control (absorbing/shielding) materials. In 2008 he co-founded Chengdu Jiachi with fellow professors Xie Jianliang and Liang Difei to commercialise lab work; it listed on the STAR Market in Dec 2024. He stepped down as director/chief scientist in Feb 2024 but remains controller.
interesting_fact: Elected to the Chinese Academy of Engineering in 2021; his team's domestic high-permeability magnetic substrate for phone antennas, used by Huawei and Xiaomi, reportedly broke a foreign monopoly and cut material prices to about a tenth.
deep_cut_fact: In Nov 2026 he received Sichuan's 2025 Science and Technology Outstanding Contribution Award; a middle-school classmate recalled him as diligent and 'always the first one at school each day'. In July 2026 Jiachi's founders pledged 10 million shares to UESTC.
notes: Academic first, businessman second; company is defense-related (stealth/EM materials), so media access may be limited. Chairwoman Yao Yao runs the company day to day. Hurun lists the company as 'industrial coatings' (EM functional coatings).

name: Liu Xinrong
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiahe Foods Industry Co. (Cograin; SSE: 605300)
profile: Suzhou-born Liu Xinrong founded Jiahe Foods in Wujiang in 2001 to make non-dairy creamer (plant-based fat powder), then dominated by foreign suppliers, and rode China's milk-tea boom to a 2021 Shanghai listing as the 'first creamer stock'. With his wife Tang Zhengqing he controls the company, which is now pivoting toward coffee.
interesting_fact: Jiahe built its own spray-drying production line in-house at founding; its first creamer product ran at full capacity from launch, and the company became known as China's 'king of creamer' supplying tea-drink chains.
deep_cut_fact: Liu trained in grain inspection at Jiangsu Jianghai Trade School, and after graduating at 18 worked as a counter clerk at the Songling grain station in Wujiang, then as a QC/R&D staffer in Suzhou and a technical supervisor at a dairy plant in Shantou.
notes: Shared fortune with wife Tang Zhengqing. Low media profile; route via board secretary office (board secretary Liu Xinren). Some filings misspell the email as ir@cogrian.cn.

name: Cen Guojian
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Ningbo ZhongDa Leader Intelligent Transmission Co. (SZSE: 002896)
profile: Cen Guojian (b. 1968), a Cixi motor-industry veteran, built ZhongDa Leader from his 1998 machinery partnership into a listed maker of geared motors and precision reducers (planetary, RV and harmonic) used in industrial automation and robots. He and his wife Zhou Guoying are the actual controllers; he has been chairman since 2015 and again also GM since 2023.
interesting_fact: ZhongDa Leader says it is one of the few companies mass-producing all three precision-reducer types (planetary, RV and harmonic) and sells integrated reducer+servo+drive modules, putting it in the supply chain for industrial and humanoid robots.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his own business Cen worked at Ningbo Changjiang Motor Factory and Cixi Gexin Motor Factory, then ran Zhanyun Machinery as managing partner from 1998 to 2006 before forming ZhongDa in 2006.
notes: Fortune shared with wife Zhou Guoying. No personal media presence; route via board secretary (Wu Xujun) at the published company email. Robotics/reducer angle could be a hook.

name: Tang Jianxing
current_role: Chairman, CEO and general manager, Huizhou DBG Technology Co. (SZSE: 300735)
profile: Shanghai-born Hong Kong resident Tang Jianxing (b. 1957) joined DBG Technology in Daya Bay, Huizhou as a minority shareholder in 1998 and grew it from a single-customer SMT assembly shop into an EMS provider for Huawei, Xiaomi, Samsung, Honor and others, now ranked about 14th globally. It is expanding into automotive electronics, including via the acquisition of France's All Circuits.
interesting_fact: Tang says DBG's goal is to break into the global top 10 EMS providers within 3-5 years, explicitly benchmarking itself against Jabil; the company celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a salesman at Shanghai's No. 1 Commerce Bureau (1975-82), and in May 1984 was posted by Sanyo to Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei, rising to factory manager over a decade; when the cassette-recorder business collapsed in 1997 he put his severance money into DBG.
notes: Gave a long 30th-anniversary interview to China Securities Journal (2025), so open to press. Route via board office email. Avoid the 2000s shareholder-control dispute mentioned in profiles.

name: Chai Lin
current_role: Director and chief engineer, Chengdu Ultra Pure Applied Materials Co. (SZSE ChiNext: 301717)
profile: Chai Lin (b. 1971, Chengdu) is co-controller, with his younger brother and chairman Chai Jie, of Ultra Pure Applied Materials, a maker of specialty-coated components for semiconductor etching, lithography and deposition tools. He joined in 2008 and led the shift into chip-equipment coatings from 2009; the company listed on ChiNext on 11 Aug 2026 and soared over 600% on day one.
interesting_fact: Ultra Pure says it is one of the few Chinese suppliers of key coated parts for 5nm-and-below etching equipment, taking on Korea's KoMiCo and Japan's Tocalo; BYD is its fourth-largest shareholder and saw a ~15x paper gain at the IPO.
deep_cut_fact: A UESTC graduate, Chai Lin was an assistant engineer at UESTC's electronics experiment centre, an engineer at the Chengdu Precision Optics Engineering Research Center, and a senior engineer at Leybold Optics' Beijing office before joining his brother's company.
notes: Technical co-founder rather than the public face; brother Chai Jie (chairman/GM) is the main spokesperson. Hurun's 'sensors' label is loose: business is semiconductor-equipment coatings. No published IR email found yet (newly listed); check cninfo for 301717.

name: Yu Awu
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Mingpai Jewellery Co. (SZSE: 002574); chairman, Zhejiang Sun & Moon (Riyue) Jewelry Group
profile: Yu Awu (b. 1941), a senior economist from Shaoxing, built the Sun & Moon (Riyue) group from a local gold-jewellery factory into one of China's largest jewellery makers; its listed arm Mingpai Jewellery (gold, platinum, diamonds) is controlled by him and his son Yu Tuliang. The family group also spans property and finance, and Mingpai has diversified into PV solar-cell manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Mingpai Jewellery, best known for gold jewellery, launched a 20GW 'new-energy PV cell smart manufacturing' project through its subsidiary Zhejiang Riyue Solar Energy Technology, a notable jewellery-to-solar pivot relevant to an energy podcast.
deep_cut_fact: From 1987 to 1995 Yu ran the Zhejiang Laofengxiang Jewellery Factory as factory director, and chaired Shaoxing County Laofengxiang Jewellery Co. until 1999, before building his own Riyue group (founded 1995). Still chairman of Mingpai at about 85.
notes: Aged ~85; son Yu Tuliang is co-controller and likely the more practical contact. Group name in Chinese: 日月集团 / 浙江日月首饰集团. The solar unit has faced asset-impairment testing, so frame the PV angle neutrally.

name: Ge Yaolun
current_role: Director and lifetime honorary chairman, Hailir Pesticides and Chemicals Group (SSE: 603639)
profile: Ge Yaolun (about 65) founded Qingdao-based Hailir, a crop-protection (pesticide) maker, after a career in Laixi's rural supply cooperatives and agri-input firms. He chaired the company through its Shanghai listing (SSE: 603639); his son Ge Jiacheng is now chairman and GM, and Ge, his wife Zhang Aiying and son jointly control the group.
interesting_fact: Hailir is a family-controlled pesticide group from Laixi, Qingdao; Ge stepped back to 'lifetime honorary chairman' and handed the chairmanship and CEO role to his son Ge Jiacheng, a former accountant at Alcatel-Lucent's Qingdao unit.
deep_cut_fact: Ge began as head of the fruit station at the Tangjiazhuang supply-and-marketing cooperative in Laixi, then deputy director of the Wangcheng co-op, and ran the fruit company of Qingdao Dongfang Peanut Group before moving into agrochemicals.
notes: Largely retired from operations; son Ge Jiacheng (chairman/GM) is the active leader. Outreach is better via the company board office.

name: Jing Shiping
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Hengmingda Electronic Technology Co. (SZSE: 002947)
profile: Jing Shiping (b. 1969) built Hengmingda from a Shenzhen packaging-printing shop into a Kunshan-based maker of precision flexible and metal structural parts for smartphones, tablets, laptops and VR/AR devices. He has chaired the listed company since 2017 and controls it with family members; it now also supplies metal structures for EV chargers, energy storage and PV inverters.
interesting_fact: Hengmingda has moved beyond consumer electronics into new energy, supplying precision metal structural parts for charging piles, battery-swap cabinets, home and C&I energy-storage systems and PV inverters to leading Chinese new-energy firms.
deep_cut_fact: Jing started out at Hong Kong's Dasheng company and the Hengmingda packaging & printing plant in Bao'an, Shenzhen, and ran Kunshan Hengmingda Packaging Materials from 1999 before pivoting the business into electronics components; he holds an MBA.
notes: Family-controlled (Jing Shiping, Jing Tianping, Jing Jingping, Xia Chen, Jing Jiang); Jing Tianping is legal rep/GM. Energy-storage component angle fits the podcast. Route via securities affairs office email.

name: Shen Huayuan
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2007-2019) as founder of 'Tailai', a hotel-management and decoration business. Searches in Chinese and English found no verifiable public record linking 沈华源 to a named Tailai company, so identity and current status could not be confirmed.
notes: Very low public footprint; dropped off Hurun after 2019. Company Chinese name unclear (泰莱/泰来). Would need business-registry lookup to identify; not recommended as an outreach priority.
